offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The evidence points to an exhausted Postgres pool in payments-api that began soon after its 21:31:28 deploy. The provider is fast, so it is not the cause.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payments-api deploy at 21:31:28 (REFUND_CONNECTION=kept) most likely makes the refund path hold Postgres pool connections and never return them. The pool drained over about a minute. From about 21:32:40, every request that needs a DB connection (POST /payments and POST /payments/{id}/refunds) waits the full pool timeout of about 5 s and then fails with psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout, returned as a 500. That gives both the 5xx rate and the p95 latency of about 6–7 s. Provider calls stay fast (p95 about 5–7 ms), so slow provider calls holding connections do not explain it, which leaves a leak. Still open: I could not see the settings before the deploy, so I cannot confirm that REFUND_CONNECTION changed in it. I did not check Postgres-side connection state or the money_check.

evidence.shows: POST /payments was healthy (201s) until 21:32:40. Then 500s rose to 5.7/s and 201s fell to 0.
payments-api alone was redeployed at 21:31:28, about 70 s before the failures began, with REFUND_CONNECTION=kept. Every other service has been unchanged since 21:30:01.
Every recent payments-api error on POST /payments is a PoolTimeout (psycopg_pool).

A failing request spends about 5 s waiting between its Redis idempotency SET and the error. It makes no DB or provider span, then ends in 500 with error.type psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout, which means it never got a pool connection.
Mean latency for both /payments and /refunds jumped from about 0.03 s to about 6 s at the same moment (21:32:40), which points to a shared DB pool.
Provider call p95 stayed at about 5–7 ms, so the provider is not slow and is not what holds the connections.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to the settings it ran before the 21:31:28 deploy, so refunds release their DB connection again. Recreating the container also empties the leaked pool. Afterwards, confirm that the 5xx rate and latency on /payments recover and that pool timeouts stop. Then run money_check to make sure no payment or refund was left half-done, for example idempotency keys set in Redis while the request failed.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container restarts, and requests in flight fail during that window (clients can retry with their idempotency keys). If the leak is not caused by the deploy, the restart only frees the pool for a while and the errors will come back.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy payments-api with the current settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, REFUND_CONNECTION=kept) from the same image, sha256:6de373c2cd8a.
